mainTopic: The golden gifts of מונבז המלך and הילני המלכה to the בית המקדש, and what we can learn from them
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's discussion of the משנה about the gifts of מונבז המלך and his mother הילני to the בית המקדש. First, אביי explains that the gold handles מונבז made were knife handles. A ברייתא lists knife handles separately, so אביי explains that the 'handles of vessels' there were the handles of axes and hatchets. Next, the גמרא teaches that הילני's gold chandelier flashed at sunrise and signaled the time for קריאת שמע. A ברייתא says the אנשי משמר and אנשי מעמד did not read שמע at sunrise. אביי answers that the signal was for the rest of the people of ירושלים. Finally, the גמרא tries to prove from הילני's golden tablet that one may write a partial Torah scroll for a child. ריש לקיש in the name of רבי ינאי rejects the proof, because the tablet had only the first letters of each word. Two ברייתות are brought to challenge him: the first is answered by rereading one word, and the answer to the second begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי: the gold handles were knife handles
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the gold 'handles of vessels' that מונבז made for יום הכיפורים were the handles of knives.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It means the handles of knives.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is explaining which kind of handles the משנה is talking about when it says מונבז made gold handles for the יום הכיפורים vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gold is too soft to make a knife blade, so a fully gold knife makes no sense. אביי says only the handles of the knives were gold. The blade stayed a strong metal.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
With the handles of knives.
phrases.notes: The blades could not be gold, so only the handles were.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה (on the previous amud) that מונבז made the handles of the יום הכיפורים vessels of gold.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case: the handles belonged to knives
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think whole gold knives were meant, which would be useless for slaughter.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the knife handles were made of gold.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists knife handles separately from vessel handles
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists 'handles of vessels' and 'handles of knives' as two separate items. This suggests that the משנה's 'handles of vessels' are not knife handles.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: He also made the bases of vessels, the grips of vessels, the handles of vessels, and the handles of knives of יום הכיפורים, of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists 'handles of vessels' and then separately 'handles of knives.' That suggests knives are not counted as 'vessels' here. If so, the משנה's 'handles of vessels' must mean something other than knife handles, against אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised an objection (from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
He also made the bases of vessels,
and the grips of vessels, and the handles of vessels,

phrases.aramaic: וִידוֹת סַכִּינִין שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁל זָהָב.
phrases.english: and the handles of knives of Yom Kippur, of gold.
phrases.notes: Knife handles are listed separately from 'handles of vessels.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אַף הוּא עָשָׂה כַּנֵּי כֵלִים
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that 'handles of vessels' means knife handles
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists knife handles as an extra item beyond 'handles of vessels.' So 'handles of vessels' cannot mean knife handles.

steps.title: אביי: the vessel handles were axe and hatchet handles
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the 'handles of vessels' in the ברייתא were the handles of axes and hatchets.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי explained it: With the handles of axes and hatchets.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. He explains which other tools 'handles of vessels' refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Axes and hatchets are like knives in one way: their blades must be strong metal, not gold. So 'handles of vessels' means the handles of these tools, and knife handles are a separate item. The basic idea stays the same: gold was used only for handles of tools whose blades must be hard.

phrases.english: Abaye explained it:
With the handles of axes and hatchets.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source: 'handles of vessels' means handles of axes and hatchets
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the ברייתא lists knife handles separately, its 'handles of vessels' could not be knife handles. That seemed to contradict אביי's explanation that the gold handles were for tools whose blades cannot be gold.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Handles of vessels' means axe and hatchet handles, and knife handles are listed separately.
steps.whatToRemember: מונבז made gold handles for tools whose blades must be strong: knives, axes, and hatchets.

steps.title: The משנה about הילני המלכה's golden chandelier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: הילני, the mother of מונבז, made a gold chandelier.
steps.simpleTranslation: הילני his mother made a gold chandelier, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה so it can discuss it. This line sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'וכו׳' tell us this is a quote of the משנה, not a new statement. The chandelier hung above the entrance of the היכל. Now the גמרא will add information about it.

keyTerms.meaning: etc. (signals a quote of the משנה)

phrases.english: Helene his mother made
a gold chandelier, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵילֶנִי אִמּוֹ עָשְׂתָה נִבְרֶשֶׁת שֶׁל זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הילני donated a gold chandelier to the מקדש.

steps.title: The chandelier's sparks showed the time for קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when the sun rose, the chandelier reflected sparks of light. That told everyone it was time for קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: When the sun shone, sparks came out from it, and everyone knew that the time for reciting שמע had arrived.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains what the chandelier was used for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The polished gold caught the first rays of sunrise and flashed. People in ירושלים used this flash as a signal that the time for the morning שמע had begun.

phrases.english: It was taught:
At the time when the sun shines (rises),
sparks come out from it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the chandelier, which reflects the sunlight.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַכֹּל יוֹדְעִין שֶׁהִגִּיעַ זְמַן קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע.
phrases.english: and everyone knows that the time for reciting Shema has arrived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds information about the chandelier quoted in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The chandelier's sparks at sunrise signaled the time for קריאת שמע.

steps.title: The people in the מקדש did not say שמע at sunrise
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that one who reads שמע with the אנשי משמר or the אנשי מעמד has not fulfilled his obligation. The משמר read too early and the מעמד read too late. So who used the sparks as a signal?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: One who reads שמע in the morning with the men of the priestly watch or the men of the Israelite watch has not fulfilled his obligation, because the men of the priestly watch rise early and the men of the Israelite watch delay!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 5 with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people in the מקדש were the אנשי משמר and the אנשי מעמד. Neither group read שמע at sunrise. The כהנים read early to be ready for the עבודה, and the מעמד read late. So it seems nobody there was using the sunrise signal.

keyTerms.meaning: the כהנים on duty in the מקדש that week
the ישראלים who stood with the קרבן that week
he did not fulfill his obligation

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who reads Shema in the morning
with the men of the priestly watch, or the men of the Israelite watch —
has not fulfilled his obligation,
because the men of the priestly watch rise early,
phrases.notes: They read before the proper time so they can begin the עבודה.

phrases.english: and the men of the Israelite watch delay!
phrases.notes: They read after the proper time.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע שַׁחֲרִית עִם אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the chandelier signaled the time of שמע for 'everyone'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The groups present in the מקדש did not read at sunrise. So the sunrise signal seems to serve no one.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say these groups were wrong to read at those times. It only says that someone else who copies their timing does not fulfill his obligation.

steps.title: אביי: the signal was for the rest of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the sparks were a signal for the ordinary people of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: For the rest of the people in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the challenge by saying who the signal was for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Everyone' in the ברייתא does not include the משמר and the מעמד, who had their own schedules. It means the general population of ירושלים, who read שמע at the proper time.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
For the rest of the people in Jerusalem.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the audience of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Everyone' seemed to mean the people inside the מקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The signal was for the general public of ירושלים, not the משמר or the מעמד.
steps.whatToRemember: The chandelier's flash at sunrise told the people of ירושלים that the time for שמע had come.

steps.title: The משנה: הילני also made a golden tablet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: הילני also made a golden tablet with the פרשת סוטה written on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And she also made a tablet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה to discuss it. This step sets up the inference that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the משנה, the tablet had the פרשת סוטה written on it. The כהן could copy from it when writing the סוטה's scroll. The גמרא will now ask what this teaches about writing partial Torah texts.

keyTerms.meaning: the Torah section about the סוטה

phrases.english: And she also made a tablet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הילני donated a golden tablet with the פרשת סוטה.

steps.title: Proof that a partial scroll may be written for a child
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the tablet that one may write a scroll with only a section of the Torah to teach a child.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: One may write a scroll for a child to learn from.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove a הלכה from the tablet. The tablet had only one section of the Torah on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a dispute whether one may write just part of the Torah as a separate מגילה, even to teach a child. Since the tablet had only one פרשה written on it, it seems that writing a partial Torah text is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: a scroll with only part of the Torah

phrases.english: Learn from this:
One may write a scroll for a child
to learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a הלכה from the tablet of step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That a partial Torah scroll may be written to teach a child
steps.raayaSupportSource: הילני's tablet, which had only the פרשת סוטה written on it
steps.whyThisMatters: Writing a partial Torah text is debated in הלכה. A proof from the מקדש practice would decide that dispute.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the tablet had only first letters
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש in the name of רבי ינאי rejects the proof. The tablet had only the first letters of each word, not the full text.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי ינאי: With אלף בית (only initial letters).
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש rejects the proof from step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tablet had only the first letter of each word, as a memory aid. So it was not really a written section of the Torah. Because of this, it proves nothing about writing a partial Torah scroll for a child.

keyTerms.meaning: ריש לקיש, a leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל
רבי ינאי, ריש לקיש's teacher here
letters only, i.e. the first letter of each word

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yannai:
With alef-beit.
phrases.notes: Only the first letter of each word was written on the tablet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַנַּאי: בְּאָלֶף בֵּית
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not rule on whether writing a partial scroll for a child is allowed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the tablet had full words. It had only initial letters, so it was not a real written Torah section.
steps.whatToRemember: הילני's tablet cannot prove that a partial Torah scroll may be written for a child, because it had only the first letters of the words.
steps.confusionAlert: The question of writing a scroll for a child is not decided here. Only the proof from the tablet is rejected.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the scribe copied what was on the tablet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש with a ברייתא saying the scribe looks at the tablet and writes what is written there. That sounds like the tablet had the full text.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: When the scribe writes the סוטה scroll, he looks and writes what is written on the tablet!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to challenge ריש לקיש's claim that the tablet had only first letters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the scribe copies 'what is written' on the tablet, then the tablet must have held the full words. You cannot write a whole scroll by copying first letters only. So the ברייתא seems to contradict ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, usually from a ברייתא
Writes, here the scribe writing the סוטה scroll

steps.confusionAlert: The 'he' who writes is the scribe (or כהן) preparing the סוטה scroll that is later erased into the water. It is not הילני.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
When he writes (the סוטה scroll),
he looks and writes what is written on the tablet!
phrases.notes: This implies the full text was on the tablet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's rejection in Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that the tablet held only first letters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Copying 'what is written' on the tablet means the full text was there.

steps.title: Read it as 'like what is written' on the tablet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the reading of the ברייתא to 'like what is written.' The tablet only reminded the scribe of the passage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: he looks and writes like what is written on the tablet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by adjusting one word of the ברייתא: from 'what' (מָה) to 'like what' (כְּמָה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'like what,' the scribe is not copying letter by letter. He looks at the first letters on the tablet to remember the passage, then writes the full words. This fits ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead. The גמרא is changing the reading of a source.

phrases.english: Say instead: he looks and writes
like what is written on the tablet.
phrases.notes: The tablet is a memory aid, not a full copy.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Change the reading of the ברייתא (אֵימָא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The scribe copied the full text straight from the tablet.
steps.terutzMaskana: The scribe used the tablet's first letters to remember and wrote the full words himself.

steps.title: A second ברייתא quotes the full verses on the tablet
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says what was on the tablet and quotes full phrases from the פסוקים of סוטה. That looks like more than first letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from another ברייתא: When he writes, he looks and writes what is written on the tablet. And what is written on the tablet? 'If a man lay with you,' 'and if he did not lay,' 'if you strayed,' 'if you did not stray'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger ברייתא that actually lists the words on the tablet, attacking ריש לקיש again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'like what is written' answer does not work here. This ברייתא spells out the tablet's content as whole phrases from the פסוקים. So it seems the tablet had real words, not only first letters.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If a man lay with you,' from the כהן's oath to the סוטה
You strayed, meaning you were unfaithful
And what is written? The ברייתא spells out the content.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
When he writes,
he looks and writes what is written on the tablet,
and what is written on the tablet?
'If a man lay with you' ['and if he did not lay'],
'if you strayed,' 'if you did not stray'!
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:19–20. This sounds like full words on the tablet.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: כְּשֶׁהוּא כּוֹתֵב רוֹאֶה וְכוֹתֵב מָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּטַּבְלָא, וּמָה כָּתוּב בַּטַּבְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new and stronger challenge that the אֵימָא answer of Step 12 cannot solve
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that the tablet held only first letters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא quotes whole phrases from the tablet, so full words seem to have been written on it.

steps.title: The answer begins: 'There...'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer with the word הָתָם ('there'). The answer is finished on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is beginning its answer to the second ברייתא. Only the first word, 'there,' appears on this amud. The rest of the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'There' points back to the second ברייתא. The גמרא is about to explain how the tablet was written so that this ברייתא can still fit ריש לקיש's view. Wait for the next passage to see exactly how.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in that case or that source

phrases.english: There (it was written...)
phrases.notes: The answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the קשיא of Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the case of the second ברייתא (completed on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves the tablet held full words.
steps.terutzMaskana: The full resolution appears on the next amud.
